messages:
olivia_k: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a replacement for our canary flow called 'traffic gates' (state-machine-driven rollout with multi-metric gates). Wanted to capture tradeoffs and outline the interface boundary between router + runtime.

jamal: TL;dr?

olivia_k: Short: move decisioning out of the runtime, express rollout as a state machine (Gates: perf, correctness, cost) that the router consults. Runtime only exposes model-variant health + fast fallbacks.

priya: I'm +1, but how do we evaluate "correctness" automatically? That's fuzzy.

olivia_k: Good point. For correctness gate we want signal combos: top-k model error increases, hallucination detectors (batch evals), and user-visible regression rate (client-reported errors). Not perfect — gate should be conservative.

ryan: How do we prevent noisy signals from flipping gates rapidly?

olivia_k: We use sliding windows + outlier-resistant aggregation (median of per-minute buckets) and require sustained breaches for N minutes. Also add a minimum sample size check.

sylvia: Architecturally where does this state live? In the router? In a separate service? DB?

olivia_k: Separate Rollout Service (long-term). It owns state machine, evaluation, audit logs, and APIs. Router queries it (fast cache) for per-route routing decision. Runtime remains simple: accept model id and serve; expose health/metrics and a fallback endpoint.

jamal: That means eventual consistency between Rollout Service and router caches — acceptable?

olivia_k: Yes, we accept small staleness. Router caches TTL=2s for hot routes, fallback to local policy if unanswered. For emergencies we provide a manual override endpoint that the oncall can hit to force rollback.

priya: Can we see a rough config example?

olivia_k: Sure — pseudo-yaml: ```
rollout: 
  id: route-embed-v2 
  steps: 
    - name: smoke 
      percent: 1 
      gates: 
        - metric: p95_latency_ms 
          threshold: 120 
          window_mins: 5 
        - metric: error_rate 
          threshold: 0.01 
          window_mins: 10 
    - name: ramp 
      percent: 20 
      gates: 
        - metric: upstream_quality_regressions 
          threshold: 0.005 
        - metric: token_rate_cost_increase 
          threshold: 0.1 
      rollback_policy: immediate_on_gate_fail 
```

ryan: rollback_policy immediate_on_gate_fail = scary. We should support soft-fail (reduce %) before full rollback.

olivia_k: Agree. We can support configurable policies: soft_reduce (halves percent), full_rollback, or route_to_fallback_variant. Defaults: soft_reduce then evaluate.

sylvia: What are fallback variants? Model smaller quantized variant? Older checkpoint? Region?

olivia_k: All of the above. We rank fallbacks by preservation of semantics then cost. Default: same-region model-variant -> older checkpoint -> lower-cost quantized -> cross-region -> queued fallback. Router will prefer cheaper/fast fallbacks if enabled by tenant policy.

jamal: Edge case: state machine decides to fallback due to hallucination detector spike. But client already saw bad outputs. Do we surface events for SRE/CS?

olivia_k: Yes — Rollout Service emits events (audit + webhooks) and creates an incident draft to triage. We also tag traces so user-facing errors can be correlated.

priya: How do we test? Staging flow? A/B experiments?

olivia_k: Suggestion: staged tests: unit + integration tests for the state machine, an emulation harness that replays traffic to rollout service and router, and a canary-sim environment that does deterministic A/B for a subset of internal traffic. Also automated chaos tests (metric flaps) to validate smoothing code.

ryan: Performance: router needs low latency for decision path. Extra RPC to Rollout Service could add cost.

olivia_k: We'll deploy fast in-memory cache in router with pub/sub invalidation from rollout service. First pass: router asks local cache, if miss syncs, otherwise fallback to conservative local policy. Benchmarks suggest ~500ns median extra if cache-hit, ~2ms on cold sync.

sylvia: What about ACLs / tenant isolation for private deployments?

olivia_k: Rollout Service supports per-tenant rollout scopes; for Private deployments the service can run in-customer VPC or we provide a local mode (state kept in customer DB). API surface stays same.

jamal: Long-term refactor: are we comfortable moving logic out of runtime? Ops may resist if it increases cross-service complexity.

olivia_k: Tradeoff: runtime simplicity vs more moving parts. Advantage: router + rollout can orchestrate multi-model rollouts (model + quantization + region) which runtime alone cannot. We'll mitigate complexity with clear owner boundaries, SDKs, and stable protobuf API.

priya: Action items?

olivia_k: Proposed next steps: 
1) Write short RFC with state-machine definition + config schema (this week)
2) Prototype Rollout Service minimal API + router cache (2 sprints)
3) Add emulator harness + chaos tests (3 sprints)
4) Pilot on non-critical embedding routes, then expand.

ryan: I'll volunteer to prototype router cache + invalidation.

sylvia: I'll draft the per-tenant privacy model and customer-local-mode notes.

jamal: Ops / oncall — want to review rollback_button UX. @oncall-bot can you add this to next SRE sync?

oncall-bot: Added: SRE sync agenda item "Rollout Service: rollback UX & emergency flows" on next meeting.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline note: remember to gate rollout-service changes with migration window. DB migrations must be backward compatible. :warning:

olivia_k: Thanks all. I'll open the RFC and link the prototype issue. Comments welcome in the RFC — aim to get consensus before we start prototyping. :thumbsup:
